subject: Proposal: time-sliced throughput windows for Dedicated pool — NectarCloud
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@nectarcloud.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: NectarCloud SRE <sre@nectarcloud.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 10:18:00 -0400
Subject: Performance concerns during nightly batch window / dedicated capacity request

Hi Rafael,

Quick note from our SRE team — over the last three weeks we've seen recurring 99th-percentile latency spikes during our nightly ingestion window (roughly 01:00–04:00 UTC). I attached a trimmed usage export (usage_report_sep.csv) showing token volumes and p95/p99 distributions.

Current setup: Dedicated pool with reserved instances you provisioned in August. Problem: when our nightly orchestration kicks off (large batch of short prompt encoding + embeddings), overall throughput is fine but tail latency spikes to 400–600ms intermittently which breaks our downstream pipelines. Our SLA requires consistent tail-latency behavior during the batch run.

Can Redwood provide a contractual guarantee for dedicated throughput during the 01:00–04:00 UTC window (we're asking for sustained 250 RPS with p99 < 150ms for our typical payload distribution)? If not, we'd like a formal exception that includes mitigation steps, fallbacks, and any credits if targets are missed.

Also copying procurement to flag this could become a contract amendment if feasible.

Thanks,
Elena Soto
Head of Platform — NectarCloud
elena.soto@nectarcloud.com

Attachment: usage_report_sep.csv (CSV, 120KB)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@nectarcloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Performance concerns during nightly batch window / dedicated capacity request

Thanks for the data, Elena — appreciate the clear export. I reviewed the usage file and the p99 pattern. We have a proposal that might fit your use case: "time-sliced throughput windows" for Dedicated pools.

High-level idea:
- We schedule a guaranteed throughput window (e.g., 01:00–04:00 UTC) during which your reserved GPU capacity enforces stricter admission control and headroom to limit tail latency.
- Outside the window, regular reserved/shared pooling rules apply.
- The window is configurable (start/end, guaranteed RPS, rr-window size) and can be applied weekly or on specific calendar dates.

Benefits: tight tail-latency isolation at predictable times without requiring permanently overprovisioned pools. Trade-offs: tooling to coordinate preemption and a short warm-up for KV cache priming during the first 10–15 minutes of the window.

A few details I need to confirm to make a concrete SLA proposal:
- Confirm intended guaranteed throughput (you mentioned 250 RPS) and expected seq/token sizes (median and 95th).
- Are you comfortable with a soft-preemption model where best-effort non-window traffic can be paused during the window?
- Do you want credits tied to p99 misses (we can propose credit tiers)?

I'm attaching a short concept note (time_sliced_concept.pdf) and looping Marissa for SLA/pricing and Karthik for implementation constraints.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Manager — Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com

Attachment: time_sliced_concept.pdf (PDF, 85KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@nectarcloud.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2026 11:47:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Performance concerns during nightly batch window / dedicated capacity request

Hi Elena — thanks for raising this. Quick commercial framing and a draft SLA clause below that we've used as a starting point for similar time-bound guarantees. The economics are typically modest compared to full-time overprovisioning.

Proposed SLA snippet (draft):
- Windowed Throughput Guarantee: Redwood will guarantee a minimum sustained throughput of X RPS (configurable) for the customer's Dedicated pool during the scheduled time window specified in the service order.
- Latency Target: During the window, 99th-percentile tail latency for single-turn text generation requests will not exceed 150ms for request sizes up to 512 tokens.
- Measurement and Credits: If Redwood fails to meet the guaranteed throughput or latency target for more than 3 non-consecutive windows in a 30-day period, customer will receive a credit of 10% of the monthly Dedicated fee for that month, per missed window (capped at 50% for the month).
- Canary & Acceptance: A 7-day canary period will precede the effective SLA. Acceptance criteria: stable throughput within 5% of target and p99 within agreed bound for 5/7 days.

If you confirm X=250 RPS and the 512-token sizing, I can put together a formal amendment we can route through legal/procurement. We can also offer a price uplift for guarded windows (typically +8–12% of the monthly reserved fee depending on headroom).

Next steps: Rafael/Karthik, please confirm technical feasibility and any additional mitigations we should include.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: proposed_sla_draft.docx (DOCX, 42KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Elena Soto <elena.soto@nectarcloud.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Sep 2026 14:32:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Performance concerns during nightly batch window / dedicated capacity request

Putting in infra perspective and a suggested implementation pattern. Quoting Rafael

> We schedule a guaranteed throughput window (e.g., 01:00–04:00 UTC) during which your reserved GPU capacity enforces stricter admission control and headroom to limit tail latency.

Implementation notes:
1) Admission control: we will enforce a token-based admission token bucket scoped to the tenant during the window. This guarantees steady-state dispatch rate and prevents sudden spikes from saturating the injector threads.
2) KV cache warm-up: to avoid the 10–15 min tail at window start, we recommend a short pre-warm phase where we replay recent prefixes from your telemetry into the serving layer; this can be scripted and run up to 30 minutes before the window.
3) Preemption semantics: soft-preemption: we deprioritize non-window tenant work (push to best-effort scheduler) but do not terminate in-flight requests. Hard-preemption (kill) is avoidable except for severe incidents.
4) Fairness: if multiple tenants request overlapping windows on the same physical pool, we use a priority-based allocation (customer SLA tier > reserved commit > burst). We will surface a per-window headroom metric to customers via the Console so you can monitor effective capacity.

Config sketch (for engineering):
capacity.window {
  start: "01:00"
  end: "04:00"
  timezone: "UTC"
  guaranteed_rps: 250
  token_bucket_capacity: 500
  preemption: "soft"
  kv_prewarm: true
}

Expected impact: other tenants may see higher queuing outside windows if resources are tight; that is why we recommend a small headroom buffer (10–15%) and a canary week.

Rafael/Marissa: if you want I can prepare an ops-runbook describing steps to run a canary and how we calculate credits for missed windows.

—Karthik
Head of Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

- Latency target: p99 < 150ms for requests <= 512 tokens
- Canary: 7 days before the amendment goes live
- Credits: draft terms you proposed look reasonable, procurement will confirm exact wording and PO.

Please route a formal amendment + runbook and loop in our procurement (procurement@nectarcloud.com). We have a standard PO template (attached) — please let me know if you need billing info or a change in payment terms.

Next steps: Rafael — can you put the formal amendment on your side and include Karthik's runbook and the prewarm checklist? If procurement needs an uplift number for the monthly fee for the guarded window, Marissa — please provide your recommended uplift so we can include it in the PO.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
